hook_text: A steel key goes into blue water and comes out copper. No paint, no dip, just a battery.
clip_script: Electroplating grows a thin metal coat with electricity. Chrome taps, nickel coins, gold connectors, zinc screws. The cell: a solution of the coating metal's salt, a strip of that metal on plus, the object on minus, a low-volt battery. Copper ions in the solution are pulled to the negative key and land as copper. The strip dissolves to replace them. Rules: key spotless, current low, key facing the strip, not touching. Sand it, wash it, do not touch it, wire it, wait ten minutes: pink. Swap the leads and nothing lands. Gloves, glasses, wash your hands, keep the blue for next time.
visual_style: Whiteboard jar with blue solution, a copper strip on plus and a key on minus; ions drifting across and landing; the strip thinning; a reversed-leads jar with a cross; a gloves and glasses icon.
pacing: Uses, four parts, ions cross, rules, method, reverse test, safety.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch the plating cell with its four parts labelled before the practical.
